## Overview

At the beginning of all things, there were three primordial entities. They are simply referred to as **A**, **B**, and **C** — the Originals. Their true names were never known to mortals. Power was perfectly balanced between the three of them.

Together, they created everything that exists: the outer planes, the inner planes, the material plane, and all the races and creatures that inhabit them.

## The Schism

Despite having created the mortal races together, **A** and **C** came to believe that creation was flawed. They wanted to destroy every mortal race and begin again from scratch — a clean slate. The accidental byproduct of free will was unacceptable to them; they wanted beings who would worship without question.

**B** disagreed. B saw value in what they had made and refused to consent to annihilation. However, being only one against two, B was outnumbered and could not prevent A and C from enacting their will through force.

## The Sacrifice

Unable to stop A and C through direct confrontation, **B chose a different path**. B sacrificed itself — shattering its own form and scattering its body, essence, and power across all of creation. This act suffused the cosmos with arcane energy, gave rise to magic, and seeded the material plane with precious metals and gemstones.

With B's sacrifice, mortals were given the means to defend themselves. B did not sacrifice to counter a specific plan — the invasion had not yet been conceived — but to give mortals a **general fighting chance** to survive and resist whatever A and C would attempt.

### The Balance of Reality

Before B's sacrifice, only A and C held genuine power over creation. B's act distributed power beyond the Originals for the first time, creating the **Weave** as a permanent, independent magical field available to all living beings.

The power B dispersed across all mortal races and planes is **equivalent** to the power A and C later concentrated into the 10 gods — but B's power is spread across billions of beings, while A and C's is concentrated in only 10. This is why mortals, collectively, could theoretically challenge the gods.

## The Protective Shield

As a safety net, B's sacrifice also implemented a protective effect on all planes of existence, lasting 100 years. The shield impedes direct influence from an Original source: because the gods are shattered forms of Originals A and C, neither A, nor C, nor any of the gods could directly interfere with the planes — and therefore with the development of the mortal races — while the shield held.

After those 100 years, the protective effect diminished, though it never vanished entirely. Working through its weakened protection, the gods eventually managed to open the planar rifts and execute their invasion plan against the mortal races.

## Aftermath — The Plan Enacted

After B's sacrifice, **A and C subdivided themselves** into lesser celestial beings — what would later be known as the gods. This was a strategic choice: by becoming many, they could better manage, monitor, and manipulate the mortal races who now possessed the gift of magic.

The power A and C gave to the gods was equivalent to the power B dispersed across all mortals — but concentrated and condensed in only 10 beings. Each god received a vast but **limited** amount of power that depletes over time when used, and is replenished by mortal worship.

True to their original intent, A and C's fragments (the gods) soon enacted the genocide they had always wanted. They struck a pact with the powers of the Abyss, Nine Hells, Shadowfell, and Feywild, opened planar breaches along the coast of Kythoria, and unleashed the monster invasion upon the mortal races — an event that would come to be known as **The Abominable End**.

## Secrets

The gods actively hide the truth about the Originals. Mortals do not know that their deities were once part of two primordial entities, nor do they know that B sacrificed itself to give them magic. This truth, if discovered, could unravel the foundations of faith across the world.
